findings: The causal account is structurally plausible and its claimed ancestry is real: account commit 9815098d is an ancestor of implementation commit faa256fa, and that implementation is an ancestor of the replayed head 7527ab79. Static inspection found no fixture-shaped label checks, golden-data reads, coordinate-keyed SVG surgery, comparator changes, or new unexplained constants in the reviewed change.

Java's relevant path matches the account: TextBlockExporter12026 computes one document-wide scale factor from dpi and explicit scale, and UGraphicSvg writes the already-scaled geometry. There is no Java lexer that scans comment text to decide whether later SVG primitives should be scaled.

The apostrophe-bearing dpi held-outs pass through the no-oracle product path. That supports the narrow claim that xml-comment-safe tag boundary handling prevents an apostrophe in a non-element span from swallowing later geometry and leaving it unscaled.

The mechanism still cannot be accepted because fresh explicit-scale held-outs fail in a way the account does not close. Both checker_scale_cluster_head_apos and its no-apostrophe control diverge on the same package outline path: Rust rewrites arc flags like `A6.5625,6.5625 0 0 1 ...` to `A6.5625,6.5625 0 0 1.75 ...`, which means scale_path_d currently multiplies SVG elliptical-arc flags along with coordinates.

Because the failure reproduces after removing every apostrophe from the same topology, it is not evidence against the comment-boundary claim itself; it is independent residue in the broader explicit-scale model. Per the T14 review rule, that still forces a rejected verdict for this latest checker record.

Raw SVG inspection shows the reviewed change does preserve the apostrophe-bearing Rust comments themselves rather than swallowing them into a giant unscaled span. However, Rust class comments are not byte-identical to Java's current outputs even on passing cases: Rust emits display-label comments such as `<!--class O'Brien Relay-->`, while Java emits alias-based comments such as `<!--class Relay-->`. That residue predates this checker change and means the account's byte-preservation language should not be read as present-day Java byte parity on actual class comments.
